front: What are SAT "red flag" phrases for wordiness?
back: "In order to" (→to), "due to the fact that" (→because), "has the ability to" (→can), "at this point in time" (→now), "for the purpose of" (→to/for), "it is important to note" (→delete).
hint: Long phrases that can be replaced with one word

front: What does "concise" mean on the SAT?
back: Saying the same thing in fewer words. The correct choice keeps all the meaning and uses the fewest words to do it.

front: How do you answer a "most concise" question?
back: Cross out any choice that leaves out part of the meaning, then pick the shortest choice that is left.
A phrase that says the same thing twice, like "free gift" or "combined together." One of the words can be deleted with no loss of meaning.

front: Give three examples of redundant phrases.
back: Free gift, past history, and combined together. Others include "the reason is because" and "in the year 1937" instead of "in 1937."
